nodes.title: Dehumanization
nodes.text: Denying people their full humanity: treating them as objects, problems, threats or numbers, so that harming, controlling or erasing them starts to seem acceptable.

nodes.title: Indigenous Peoples
nodes.text: Colonial policy in Canada tried to erase Indigenous identity, culture and self-determination.

nodes.title: Residential Schools
nodes.text: 1880s to 1996. More than 150,000 First Nations, Inuit and Métis children were taken from their families. Languages were forbidden and children were punished for speaking them.

nodes.title: The Indian Act, 1876
nodes.text: The government decided who legally counted as 'Indian' and banned ceremonies like the potlatch from 1884 to 1951.

nodes.title: “The Indian problem”
nodes.text: “I want to get rid of the Indian problem.” Duncan Campbell Scott, 1920. People reduced to a problem to be solved.

nodes.title: Sixties Scoop
nodes.text: Thousands of Indigenous children were taken into care and adopted into non-Indigenous homes, cut off from family and culture.

nodes.title: MMIWG
nodes.text: Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls. The 2019 National Inquiry called the violence a genocide.

nodes.title: Black Canadians
nodes.text: Anti-Black racism in Canada is often hidden behind the story that Canada was only ever a safe haven.

nodes.title: Slavery in Canada
nodes.text: Enslaved Black people were bought and sold in New France and British North America until slavery was abolished in 1834.

nodes.title: Africville, Halifax
nodes.text: A Black community denied city services for decades, then demolished in the 1960s. Residents were relocated, some of them in garbage trucks.

nodes.title: Viola Desmond, 1946
nodes.text: Arrested and jailed for sitting in the whites-only section of a theatre in New Glasgow, Nova Scotia.

nodes.title: Carding & street checks
nodes.text: Black people were stopped and documented by police far more often than white people. They were treated as suspects first and people second.

nodes.title: Mental Health
nodes.text: People living with mental illness have been labelled, locked away and talked about as less than whole people.

nodes.title: Asylums & institutions
nodes.text: Patients were isolated from society and stripped of their rights, privacy and control over their own lives.

nodes.title: Language
nodes.text: “Crazy.” “Psycho.” “Insane.” Words like these turn a person into a label.

nodes.title: Stigma
nodes.text: Shame and fear stop people from getting help. Illness is seen as weakness or danger instead of something to treat.

nodes.title: Intergenerational trauma
nodes.text: The trauma of residential schools still affects the mental health of survivors' children and grandchildren.
